No disqualifier applies: it is a single named award, the company is profitable and growing, and the packet shows no distress.

result.mechanism: Firm order from NPCI (INR 267.58 cr excl. GST) for supply, installation, testing and commissioning of server infrastructure at NPCI data centres, plus seven years of maintenance and support.
result.rationale: A firm NPCI order of INR 267.58 cr over seven years is 18.8% of TTM revenue INR 1,424 cr on the rule's total-versus-annual basis (about 2.7% a year if spread evenly). Similar INR 140-750 cr firm wins recur, so the order is routine, but market cap INR 1,571 cr is 1.10x TTM revenue, so the cheap-valuation exception applies and the order is decided as non-routine, with TTM revenue growth of +12.4%. No disqualifier; the company is profitable (TTM PAT INR 85 cr) with low finance cost. Borderline on the multi-year basis, so confidence is LOW.
result.what_changed: A firm multi-year order was received on 2026-07-28. Similar firm wins recur (Union Bank INR 214 cr Feb 2024, NABARD INR 233 cr Apr 2024, Bank of Maharashtra INR 142.55 cr Sep 2024, RBI INR 249 cr Dec 2025, RBI INR 751 cr May 2026), so on routine-flow grounds the order is business as usual. Market cap is 1.10x TTM revenue, so the cheap-valuation exception applies and the order is decided as non-routine.
contradictions: Stated value is a seven-year total; spread evenly it is about INR 38 cr a year, about 2.7% of TTM revenue. Total-versus-annual basis per rule step 1 gives 18.8%
Routine: similar INR 140-750 cr orders were won in 2024, 2025 and 2026; the decision relies on the cheap-valuation exception (P/S 1.10 below 1.5x)
TTM operating margin 10.2% is just above the 10% thin-margin threshold, so only the cheap-valuation exception applies
result.next_milestone: Supply, installation and commissioning of the server infrastructure at NPCI data centres, then recognition of seven years of maintenance revenue

result.mechanism: Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) software and solution order from the Reserve Bank of India, awarded 30 Dec 2025 at INR 249.15 crore, delivered with integrated OEM tools (IBM, Elastic, Hazelcast, JFrog). It is a data-centre and software-platform award in the company's existing BFSI/PSU business.
result.rationale: 14-day freshness filter: the basis order was first announced 2025-12-30, more than 14 days before week 2026-02-09; Haiku had DEEP_RESEARCH. The INR 249.15 crore RBI Enterprise Application Platform order (awarded 30 Dec 2025) is firm and about 18.4% of TTM revenue (INR 1,351 crore). The company wins bank and PSU orders of INR 100-300 crore regularly, so it is routine, but the market cap is 0.91x TTM revenue (below 1.5x) and TTM revenue growth is +10.7%, so under the cheap-valuation exception it is decided as non-routine. No disqualifier is evident, but the order is comparable to earlier bank orders, Dec-quarter revenue growth was only +9.5%, and the execution period and margin are not stated. Order book check is in order_book_check.
result.what_changed: A single INR 249 crore central-bank order is about 18% of TTM revenue (INR 1,351 crore). It is comparable to the company's earlier INR 214-293 crore bank orders, so the change is one of scale within the existing pattern rather than a new revenue stream. The Dec-quarter revenue grew only 9.5% YoY.
contradictions: Engine's INR 249 crore 'binding' order is a valid discrete award, but its scale matches the company's 2024 bank and PSU orders of INR 214-293 crore, so the change is limited.
TTM revenue growth is +10.7% and Dec-quarter revenue growth is +9.5%; the order is not yet visible in reported revenue.
Dec-quarter finance cost rose to INR 6.46 crore from INR 3.40 crore a year earlier; small in absolute terms.
